function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity as a natural phenomenon has been known for millennia—ancient Greeks observed static sparks from amber (hence the word *elektron*). The modern scientific study of electricity began in the 17th–18th centuries with figures such as William Gilbert, who coined the term *electricus*, and later Benjamin Franklin, who popularized the word *electricity* and performed his famous kite experiment. Subsequent breakthroughs by Alessandro Volta (the voltaic pile), Michael Faraday (electromagnetic induction), and others laid the foundations for our current understanding of electrical phenomena.
